reproducibility: 5 runs x 6 topics analyzed by DOI-frequency. Overall mean pairwise Jaccard across topics = 0.823 (high reproducibility). STABLE core (>=4/5 runs) = 70 DOIs; VARIABLE (2-3/5) = 10; SPORADIC (1/5) = 16. The robust reproducible signal is the 70-DOI stable core; the 26-DOI variable+sporadic tail is run-dependent noise. The scite 'scientific-record' backbone is deterministic (byte-identical scite sub-lists across all 5 runs for T1-T4); essentially ALL variance comes from the paperclip biomedical layer and a small scite tail, concentrated in Run 3 (the high-recall outlier). Most reproducible topics: T4 (J=0.900, 0 sporadics) and T3 (J=0.883, 0 variable-tier). Least reproducible: T6 (J=0.729, short lists + 'screening' polysemy off-topic noise) and T2 (J=0.761, fast-moving arXiv preprint tail).
cross_source: Source overlap by shared DOI is exactly ZERO in every topic — scite and paperclip return disjoint DOI sets (no single DOI is returned by both engines in any topic), so the two sources are purely COMPLEMENTARY, not corroborating, at the identifier level. Division of labor is consistent: scite supplies the broad CS/physics/cheminformatics + journal record (arXiv robotics/OT preprints, classic J. Chem. Inf. Model. / J. Med. Chem. / J. Comput. Chem. shape/IFP papers, all carrying support/mentions tallies); paperclip supplies the biomedical/PMC + preprint-server layer (bioRxiv/medRxiv/chemrxiv, TPAMI, Nature Comms, plus the microscopy and neuroscience alignment literature). Per-topic stable-core source split: T1 = 8 scite-stable + 4 paperclip-stable; T2 = 7 scite + 6 paperclip (incl. Fused-GW, OTMol, Supervised-GW from paperclip); T3 = 8 scite + 8 paperclip; T4 = 7 scite + 3 paperclip; T5 = 7 scite + 3 paperclip; T6 = 3 scite + 6 paperclip (paperclip dominates the fingerprint/benchmark layer here). Net: scite anchored 41/70 stable-core papers, paperclip anchored 29/70. CONVERGENCE happens at the TOPIC/concept level even though DOIs never coincide — e.g. both sources independently populate the Gromov-Wasserstein and shape-similarity cores from different document pools — which is the strongest reproducibility signal: two independent retrieval systems agree the same sub-literatures are central. The only near-duplicate cross-source contact is content-level (same decoy-selection paper: scite chemrxiv DOI vs paperclip published DOI), confirming the two engines cover the SAME work via different identifiers rather than truly disjoint science.
per_topic_jaccard: Mean pairwise Jaccard (10 run-pairs each): T1 point-cloud-registration=0.791; T2 Gromov-Wasserstein=0.761; T3 pharmacophore/shape-VS=0.883; T4 ROCS/scaffold-hopping=0.900; T5 interaction-fingerprint/decoys=0.872; T6 pose-free/alignment-free=0.729. Cross-topic mean=0.823. Stable/variable/sporadic counts per topic: T1 12/2/7, T2 13/2/4, T3 16/0/2, T4 10/2/0, T5 10/2/1, T6 9/2/2. Run identicality: the scite-sourced sub-lists are 100% identical across all 5 runs in T1-T4 (deterministic); divergence is driven almost entirely by paperclip ordering/recall and was maximal in Run 3 (which inflated T1 to 19 and T2 to 18 entries, adding 7 and 3 sporadics respectively).
